title: The Ramsey number $r(1,l)$
statement: Let the Ramsey number $r(k,l)$ denote the least natural number $n$ such that every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains either a clique on $k$ vertices or an independent set on $l$ vertices. Then for every integer $l \ge 1$ one has $r(1,l) = 1$.
hypotheses_covered: l is a natural number with 1 ≤ l
replaced:
For example, it is easy to see that
\[r(1, l) = r(k, 1) = 1 \qquad (7.5)\]
